# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 61 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 47 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_061_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 61

**1** Jesus said: "Two will rest on a bed; one will die, one will live."

**2** Salome said: "Who are you, man? You have reclined on my couch as one from the same and eaten from my table."

**3** Jesus said to her: "I am the one who comes from what is whole. I was given from the things of my Father."

**4** Salome said: "I am your disciple."

**5** Jesus said: "Therefore I say: when someone is whole, he will be filled with light; but when he is divided, he will be filled with darkness."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**"Man"** — EMET preferred over "sir" (LOGOS): the Coptic *rome* is the word for "man/person," not a title of respect. Salome's address may carry a note of surprise or challenge.

**"What is whole"** — *petjek*: EMET and SOPHIA preserve the nominal form; PNEUMA's "undivided" is theologically interesting but substitutes a negative for a positive concept.

**"I am your disciple"** — scholarly consensus attributes this to Salome. Brackets or attribution both acceptable; SOPHIA uses attribution without brackets for readability.

**Theological Note:** The conclusion (whole leads to light / divided leads to darkness) is the interpretive key: wholeness (*teleios*) as the Thomasine ideal, versus division as spiritual death.

**Synoptic Parallels:** The Q-parallel opening (Luke 17:34) is preserved but serves as a frame for the unique Salome dialogue, which has no canonical parallel.
